Daily Kos Staff

Remember when it seemed like the most monstrous, unprecedented corruption was that, during his first term, President Donald Trump stomped all over the Emoluments Clause by owning a hotel where eager oligarchs and hangers-on could pay to stay?

Doesn’t that just seem quaint by comparison to the orgy of corruption that is Trump’s second term?

In the latest bit of grift, we’ve got another conveniently timed stock move. Early in February, Trump bought between $1 and $5 million in Axon stock—a pretty hefty purchase, even for the man who has billions of corrupt dollars at his disposal.

That big purchase came just two weeks before Immigration and Customs Enforcement posted a notice for a $220 million Taser contract, one where really only Axon would fit the bill.

It’s good to be king, particularly when you get to create a sort of vertical integration of corruption because no one is going to stop you. All you have to do is instruct your agency to create a contract where only one company fits the bill, then buy stock a couple of weeks before the request for proposals hits the government’s contracting database.

It feels really weird and really not great that we don’t even look askance anymore when the president basically behaves like a day trader, making 3,600 trades in the first quarter of 2026 alone.

Even Wall Street experts say that this was so much trading that it’s more like a hedge fund balance sheet.

And in a way, it is a hedge fund balance sheet—except it’s a hedge fund where only one person benefits. So finding out that there was yet another corrupt trade feels like it barely warrants a raised eyebrow these days.

Indeed, even getting the mainstream media to pay attention is a problem, leaving independent outlets to put together that Trump seems to have a cool little pattern where he, say, praises Apple publicly the day he buys Apple stock, or buys stock the same day he does a high-profile visit to that company.

Like when Trump bought stock in UFC’s parent company while pimping the UFC event at the White House—that one just zipped on by.

Even as CNBC broke the news about the Axon purchase, it still couldn’t bring itself to acknowledge how openly corrupt it is.

“There is no evidence Trump was involved in or had knowledge of the procurement process or that Axon knew about his stock purchase. But ethics experts said the timing alone raises red flags,” it reported.

But just because the press refuses to call it corruption doesn’t mean that it isn’t mindbendingly corrupt. And though the contract hasn’t yet been awarded to Axon, once it inevitably is, the company will have realized an exceedingly good return on investment.

Axon has spent about $2.5 million lobbying Congress to buy its products for ICE, so landing a $220 million contract from that is niiiiiice.

In fact, the company should probably thank its lucky stars that neither of Trump’s sons has gotten into tasers. Because if they had, the federal government would be sliding some no-bid contracts their way instead.

Your tax dollars are already going to Unusual Machines and Vulcan—both of which are backed by Donald Trump Jr.—and Powerus, a drone company that’s handily backed by both Don Jr. and Eric Trump.

Everyone who’s participating in this whole enterprise knows full well that Trump is lining his pockets, but they don’t care. As long as they get theirs, right?
